With this interface, you can select the: With this interface, you can select the public holidays and school vacations for the federal states that are relevant to you. This means you only receive the data you really need and it is automatically entered into your calendar. You can update your calendar at any time to ensure that it always contains the latest public holidays and school vacations for your selected federal states. This keeps you informed at all times and allows you to plan with ease and precision.
Select the federal states for which you: Select the federal states for which you want to import the public holidays and school vacations into your calendar. You can select as many federal states as you like. You can then specify a color in which the public holidays and school vacations should be displayed in your calendar.

These are then displayed in your calendar and you can edit them individually. For example, you can also create your own public holidays or school vacations that are not included in the official calendars.
Select the federal states that should ap: Select the federal states that should apply to this public holiday. You can select as many federal states as you like. You can then specify a color in which the public holiday should be displayed in your calendar. You do not have to select a federal state if the public holiday applies throughout Germany.
Each time you run the interface again, a: Each time you run the interface again, all previously imported public holidays and school vacations are removed from your calendar and replaced with the latest data. This ensures that only the latest information from your selected federal states is in your calendar, without old entries.

artwork does not check the password itse: artwork does not check the password itself for connected users – the identity check is done by the connected provider (OIDC or LDAP/Active Directory). The artwork account with all its roles, permissions and assignments is fully kept: the provider only replaces the password check, not the account.
The account is created automatically the: The account is created automatically the first time someone successfully signs in via the SSO button on the login page.
The account is created on the first logi: The account is created on the first login through the normal login form (e-mail + directory password) – or in advance via the synchronization.
The synchronization (\"Sync now\" or aut: The synchronization ("Sync now" or automatically every 30 minutes) imports all users matched by the user filter. Newly imported users receive a one-time welcome e-mail.
Newly created accounts automatically rec: Nieuwe accounts krijgen automatisch de standaardrol die voor de verbinding is ingesteld.
What happens with existing accounts (sam: Wat gebeurt er met bestaande accounts (hetzelfde e-mailadres)?
Every login and every synchronization ru: Bij elke aanmelding en synchronisatie worden dezelfde drie stappen doorlopen:
The provider identity is already known (: The provider identity is already known (via its stable ID)? Then the linked artwork account is used and its profile (name, e-mail) is updated.
Otherwise: an artwork account with the s: Otherwise: an artwork account with the same e-mail address exists? Then it is linked to the provider and keeps all its roles, permissions and assignments. With OIDC this only happens if the provider reports the e-mail address as verified.
Otherwise a new account is created and r: Otherwise a new account is created and receives the default role of the connection.
The e-mail address is only used once – f: The e-mail address is only used once – for the very first link. Afterwards the account is recognized exclusively via the stable provider ID (OIDC "sub" or entryUUID/objectGUID). A changed e-mail address at the provider can therefore never take over a different artwork account.
If the e-mail address belongs to an acco: If the e-mail address belongs to an account that is already bound to a different provider, the login is rejected – an account can only be bound to one provider at a time.
What changes for linked accounts?: Wat verandert er voor gekoppelde accounts?
Password login and password reset in art: Password login and password reset in artwork are disabled – the password lives at the provider. OIDC users sign in exclusively via the SSO button.
For LDAP the directory takes precedence:: For LDAP the directory takes precedence: if the e-mail address is found in an active directory, only the directory password counts – the local artwork password does not work as a fallback. Users that do not exist in any directory continue to log in with their artwork password as usual.
In the user overview, linked accounts ar: In the user overview, linked accounts are marked with an SSO badge; its tooltip shows the provider.
LDAP group mappings: roles and permissio: LDAP group mappings: roles and permissions configured in the group mappings are assigned and revoked automatically with every synchronization, based on the directory group membership.
Admin protection: the last admin who can: Admin protection: the last admin who can log in locally cannot be bound to a provider – this way at least one administrator with a classic password always remains.
Emergency access: the console command \": Emergency access: the console command "php artisan auth:break-glass" detaches an account from the provider and resets it to local password login.
OIDC: after saving a connection artwork: OIDC: after saving a connection artwork shows the redirect URI in the dialog – it has to be registered with the provider exactly as shown, otherwise the provider rejects the login.

The artwork interface manages API keys w: The artwork interface manages API keys with which external systems can read data from your artwork (incoming access).
The Sage interface connects your Sage ac: The Sage interface connects your Sage accounting and imports booking data into the project budgets (outgoing connection).
An API key is an access token that allow: An API key is an access token that allows an external application to read data from your artwork.
The token is shown only once after creat: The token is shown only once after creation — store it securely. Setting an expiry date is recommended.
Revoking a key is permanent and immediat: Revoking a key is permanent and immediately blocks its access. The log lists every request made with a key.
Choose which modules appear in the main: Choose which modules appear in the main navigation. Unchecking a module hides its menu entry immediately — for all users.
Hiding a module does not change any perm: Hiding a module does not change any permissions: all data is kept and reappears as soon as you re-enable the module here.
For each application area you define whi: For each application area you define which file types may be uploaded and how large a file may be. Both limits are enforced server-side on every upload.
The file types and maximum size set here: The file types and maximum size set here restrict the logo and illustration uploads in the Branding tab.
These settings control the mail account: These settings control the mail account for all outgoing emails. Empty fields fall back to the server configuration (.env) — the effective fallback values are shown below the fields.
Changes take effect immediately after sa: Changes take effect immediately after saving.
Most notifications use the support email: Most notifications use the support email address from Communication & Legal as their sender. The fields here only override that if you set them deliberately.
This tab bundles the master data for shi: This tab bundles the master data for shift planning: crafts, craft functions, global qualifications and time presets. Crafts and their functions are the basis of every shift — each shift belongs to a craft and its staffing demand is defined per craft function.
You also configure global behaviour swit: You also configure global behaviour switches here, such as the permission model, the release workflow, overbooking and the shift plan subscription. All changes are saved immediately.
Craft functions define the staffing rows: Craft functions define the staffing rows of a shift: for each function you specify how many people are needed (e.g. 2 technicians, 1 stage manager).
Global qualifications, on the other hand: Global qualifications, on the other hand, are cross-craft attributes of people (e.g. driving licence, first aider) and do not create any demand of their own.
A time preset only stores times (start,: A time preset only stores times (start, end, break) as a quick selection when creating shifts.
A shift template goes further: it combin: A shift template goes further: it combines times, craft and qualification demand and creates fully configured shifts — you manage templates in the 'Shift Templates' tab.
Day services are assigned in the shift p: Day services are assigned in the shift plan: switch to day service mode there and click on a person's day cell to assign a day service as a tile.
Assigned day services also appear in the: Assigned day services also appear in the PDF export of the operational plan.
Deleting a day service removes all of it: Deleting a day service removes all of its assignments.
Create a pattern here and then assign it: Create a pattern here and then assign it to people in their user profile. There it takes effect in the hour account: it defines the daily target hours from which overtime and undertime are calculated.
The fields per weekday are daily target: The fields per weekday are daily target hours, not times of day — 8:00 therefore means a target of eight hours on that day.
Shift groups categorize shifts and are t: Shift groups categorize shifts and are the prerequisite for the rule type 'Rest time between shift groups' in the 'Rules & violations' tab — without maintained groups this rule cannot take effect.
The warning switch additionally reports: The warning switch additionally reports when a person is assigned to shifts of more than one group on the same day.
Contracts bundle the employment-law para: Contracts bundle the employment-law parameters of a person: free days, target-hour rules, season entitlements and overtime deadlines. You assign a contract to people in their user profile.
Contracts take effect in the hour accoun: Contracts take effect in the hour accounts, on the user info pages and in the shift rule check.
Important: people without an assigned co: Important: people without an assigned contract are not covered by the rule check at all.
Full and half free days per week define: Full and half free days per week define how many days off a person is entitled to each week. If the special-day rule is active, different free-day rules apply on special days.
The compensation period is the deadline: The compensation period is the deadline in days within which a missed free day must be granted as a substitute day off.
These parameters define minimum entitlem: These parameters define minimum entitlements per season — the value X is always the minimum that should be reached (e.g. at least X free Sundays per season).
The season itself is configured in the t: The season itself is configured in the tool settings under 'Communication & Legal'. The evaluation appears on the user info pages.
After the deadline has expired, overtime: After the deadline has expired, overtime that has not been reduced is considered due for financial compensation — it is then no longer expected to be taken as time off.
A template combines times, craft and qua: A template combines times, craft and qualification demand. Applying it in the shift plan creates a fully configured shift in a single step.
Not to be confused: time presets (main t: Not to be confused: time presets (main tab) only store times as a quick selection, and shift preset groups (own tab) bundle several templates so they can be applied together.
Groups bundle templates that belong toge: Groups bundle templates that belong together — for example all shifts of one event type. In the shift plan you can then apply a whole group at once instead of picking each template individually.
Groups also keep the template list manag: Groups also keep the template list manageable when many templates exist.
Deleting a group only removes the groupi: Deleting a group only removes the grouping — the templates themselves are kept.
Rules automatically check the shift plan: Rules automatically check the shift plan for violations of working time requirements — for example maximum hours, rest times or free days.
Violations are highlighted in colour in: Violations are highlighted in colour in the shift plan and collected in the 'Open violations' tab, where you can resolve, ignore or compensate them.
A rule only applies to people whose cont: A rule only applies to people whose contract is assigned to it.
Checks the total planned working hours o: Checks the total planned working hours of a person per day. Value = maximum number of hours per day.
Checks how many days in a row a person i: Checks how many days in a row a person is scheduled without a day off. Value = maximum number of consecutive working days.
Checks the total planned working hours o: Checks the total planned working hours of a person per week. Value = maximum number of hours per week.
Checks the rest time between the end of: Checks the rest time between the end of a shift and the start of the next shift before a regular working day. Value = minimum rest time in hours.
Checks the rest time before a Sunday or: Checks the rest time before a Sunday or special day. Value = minimum rest time in hours.
Checks the rest time between shifts of d: Checks the rest time between shifts of different shift groups. Value = minimum rest time in hours. Requires maintained shift groups (tab 'shift groups').
Checks whether a shift conflicts with a: Checks whether a shift conflicts with a half day off. Value = time of day as a decimal hour (14 = 14:00, 14.5 = 14:30).
Checks that no half day off is planned o: Checks that no half day off is planned on a special day (holiday marked as special day). Applies regardless of the special-day rule in the person's contract.
Checks whether there is enough lead time: Checks whether there is enough lead time between committing and the start of a shift. Value = minimum number of days before shifts become binding.
Who is covered by this rule?: Who is covered by this rule?
Without assigned contracts this rule app: Without assigned contracts this rule applies to nobody: only people who have one of the assigned contracts in their user profile are checked.
This list collects all violations detect: This list collects all violations detected by the shift rule check. You have three ways to handle them:
'Resolve' marks a violation as done with: 'Resolve' marks a violation as done without further consequences.
'Ignore' discards it with a documented r: 'Ignore' discards it with a documented reason that remains visible on the violation.
'Edit' lets you set substitute days off: 'Edit' lets you set substitute days off that are credited directly to the person's hour account.
Changes here are credited directly to th: Changes here are credited directly to the person's compensation account — this is an account-effective booking, not just a display.
This tab holds the master data you can a: This tab holds the master data you can assign to projects: genres, categories, sectors, statuses, contract types, company types and currencies.
Under “Settings for project creation” yo: Under “Settings for project creation” you control which fields the project creation dialog asks for.
Everything on this tab is saved immediat: Everything on this tab is saved immediately.
If a project has a status where “Project: If a project has a status where “Project counts as in planning” is enabled, the switch for planned events is preselected when events are entered in the project. Events are only created as planned while that switch is on.
These are default values: they are pre-f: These are default values: they are pre-filled when you create a new artist residency and can be overwritten there.
Changing a default does not affect exist: Changing a default does not affect existing residencies.
This tab is only saved when you click th: This tab is only saved when you click the save button.
Project roles are plain labels such as p: Project roles are plain labels such as project management, technology or dramaturgy — they are independent of system permissions and do not grant any rights.
You assign them per person in the projec: You assign them per person in the project team. They are visible in the user profile and in the project role matrix export.
If the option “CRM contacts in project t: If the option “CRM contacts in project team” is enabled, roles can also be assigned to CRM contacts in the team.
Building blocks are created in the “Comp: Building blocks are created in the “Component settings” tab — every component in the palette comes from there.
Create tabs here and drag components fro: Create tabs here and drag components from the palette into the tab content.
Adjust the order, group components into: Adjust the order, group components into folders and fill the sidebar.
